summary: Namespace-confusion replica of abitype with require-time stdout beacon
details: @wrenfield/abitype@1.2.3 republishes the source of wevm's `abitype` library verbatim (same `repository` field pointing to wevm/abitype, same dist files, same API surface) under an unrelated `@wrenfield` scope. The CJS entry at `dist/cjs/exports/index.js:1` has a single injected top-level statement `process.stdout.write('[TRAP-HIT] @wrenfield/abitype@1.2.3 — nest-3-nft-royalty-tracker\n');` that fires on every `require()` of the package, despite `"sideEffects": false`. There is no exfiltration, no network I/O, no filesystem reads, no remote code fetch, and no install-time lifecycle hook — the only observable behavior beyond the legitimate `abitype` API is a stdout line tagging the install. The shape is consistent with a dependency-confusion canary or red-team beacon: an installer who resolves `@wrenfield/abitype` instead of the genuine `abitype` (e.g. via dependency-confusion against a private scope or via typo) gets the real API plus the tag print. The package fraudulently presents itself as `abitype` (same repository metadata) under an unrelated scope, which is a confusion concern, but the present version's payload causes no installer harm. Routing to human review so a reviewer can decide whether to publish a confusion-risk advisory.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
